messages:
samira: heads-up: CI reports broken fragment links that point into the SDK examples page after the mdx conversion. several references to `#python-quickstart` now 404.

ci-bot: build: docs/docusaurus: linkcheck failed (exit 2). 11 broken anchors. see https://ci.redwood/example/8123 for full log :warning:

ben: sample from the log:
```
WARNING: broken link: ../sdk/python#python-quickstart -> 404
WARNING: broken link: ../sdk/javascript#js-client-usage -> 404
```
Those fragments used to jump to inline code blocks with explicit snippet titles. mdx slugifier removed the snippet-title tokens.

jordan: i think this is the snippet/title -> slug change. during the mdx migration we switched snippet rendering which dropped the data-title attribute we relied on in link generation. result: different fragment ids.

samira: ok. surgical approach: add explicit header ids on the SDK pages where external pages link in, and add a small redirects map for common legacy anchors so external links don't break. avoid mass-renaming anchors in the rest of the docs.

ben: agree. i'll make a PR that: 1) adds `{#python-quickstart}` and `{#js-client-usage}` to the sdk pages, 2) adds `static/legacy_anchors.json` with mappings like `"/sdk/python#python-quickstart": "/sdk/python#python-quickstart"` (and any legacy variants) so docusaurus redirect plugin can pick them up.

jordan: also add a short note to CONTRIBUTING that says: "When adding code snippets that are referenced from other pages, prefer an explicit header id or add snippet-title metadata so anchors remain stable." saves future churn.

tools-bot: suggestion: consider a CI helper that parses the linkcheck output and posts candidate header ids based on nearest headings/codeblock titles. i can prototype a small script that suggests `{#...}` ids as PR comments. filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/238 to track.

ben: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4555  adds 9 explicit ids across sdk pages, a legacy anchors json, and `scripts/suggest_sdk_anchor_ids.py` which heuristically matches broken fragments to nearby headings or snippet captions.

samira: before we merge, can someone run the local repro steps? here's what i use:
```
# docusaurus local check
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm run link-check
# or run the CI container image to match the environment
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src docs-ci-image:latest sh -c "cd /src && pnpm install && pnpm run link-check"
```

jordan: ran the docker flow locally against the branch. link-check still flagged two anchors because downstream pages used slightly different wording. i updated the PR to add ids that match the external references (kept ascii kebab-case).

ben: pushed the fixes. small nit: prefer `js-client-usage` vs `javascript-client-usage` to match older links. left a tiny comment in the PR.

ci-bot: note: re-run of linkcheck will be queued after PR updates. :info:

samira: i'd rather not update all external references; redirects are safer for external links we don't control. we should only canonicalize ids inside the SDK pages.

jordan: agreed. also added a tiny smoke test in `ci/anchor_smoke_test.sh` that curls a handful of known anchors and checks for 200s. helps catch regressions after deploy.

tools-bot: posted a sample PR comment template that lists broken fragments and suggested ids; might help reviewers accept these quick fixes faster.

ben: thanks. i'll re-run CI and merge on green. after merge i'll trigger a staging deploy and run the smoke test against staging to make sure the site search and anchors index properly.

samira: nice work. follow-up item: let's catalog any anchors that are likely to be linked by external partners and add them to the legacy_anchors.json to avoid SEO / partner breakage. created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/239.

(last) jordan: merging when CI passes. appreciate the quick patch — less risky than changing the slugifier globally. :+1:
